summary.headline: GAIL Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to Rs 4,292 crore (from Rs 1,262 crore in Q4), led by gas marketing and LPG/LHC gains from West Asia price spikes.
summary.overview: GAIL reported a sharply higher Q1 FY27, with consolidated PAT (ex-minority) of Rs 4,665 crore versus Rs 1,485 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by elevated crude and LPG prices and favourable Brent index movements in gas marketing. Management flagged that the gas marketing spread is largely a timing effect from the 9-month JCC sourcing versus 3-month Brent sales and will normalise. Gas marketing PBT guidance for FY27 was held at around Rs 4,500 crore despite Q1 gas marketing PBT of Rs 3,353 crore. Transmission volumes were 122.36 MMSCMD, and FY27 transmission guidance was set at around 123 MMSCMD. The Pata petchem complex is now at 100% load after a partial restart in mid-May, and the Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda pipeline became fully operational on 31 May 2026.

segments.name: Gas marketing
segments.commentary: Volumes 93.82 MMSCMD including 8.76 MMSCMD international; Q1 PBT about Rs 3,353 crore. Qatar force majeure and 7 other cargo disruptions were covered by 8 spot cargoes. FY27 PBT guidance held at around Rs 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Natural gas transmission
segments.commentary: Volume 122.36 MMSCMD vs 118.99 MMSCMD in Q4, with shipper volumes up about 4 MMSCMD. FY27 volume guidance raised to around 123 MMSCMD. Q4 transmission cost included a provision that fell from Rs 111 crore to Rs 11 crore in Q1.

segments.name: LPG transmission
segments.commentary: Volume 1,077 TMT vs 1,114 TMT in Q4 (down ~3%) due to West Asia disruption of LPG imports.

segments.name: LHC (liquid hydrocarbons)
segments.commentary: Production rose about 20% to 232 TMT from 194 TMT after an extra 0.597 MMSCMD of New Well Gas allocation; PBT Rs 772 crore vs Rs 144 crore in Q4 and Rs 489 crore in FY26. Production is expected to stay in this range through FY27.

segments.name: Polymer (petchem)
segments.commentary: Production 51 TMT with a loss of Rs 130 crore due to gas diversion to priority sectors; plant at 100% capacity and expected to reach breakeven during FY27. Pata shifting from natural gas to ethane is being pursued.

segments.name: City gas (CGD) and GAIL Gas
segments.commentary: GAIL Gas (wholly owned) had 592 CNG stations and 7,93,684 DPNG connections as of 30 June 2026, adding 16,610 DPNG in Q1. Its Q1 turnover was Rs 3,326 crore and PAT Rs 120 crore (+3% QoQ). GAIL CGD added 20,069 DPNG connections and 3 CNG stations in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change in demand outlook given government steps to reduce LPG exposure, and how should FY28-29 demand be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PNGRB paper projecting demand rising to 297 MMSCMD by FY30 from 200 MMSCMD; said GAIL has not revised its own volumes and relies on PNGRB figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Rs 4,500 crore gas marketing guidance far below the Q1 run rate, and is further upside likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gains came from JCC 9-month vs 3-month Brent timing and a one-off Brent jump; much will cure within the year, depending on dated Brent. Guidance kept due to volatility, to be revised later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Henry Hub cross-index advantage sustain for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on Brent and Henry Hub levels; the cross-index is currently in a sweet spot, but the open volume is only about 25-30% of the 21 MMSCMD, and Pata will consume its allocated volume at 100% load.

qa_highlights.question: What is the petchem breakeven gas price and the average realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Average petchem landed gas cost was $10.54/MMBtu in Q1; breakeven at about $13-14 landed gas cost with selling price around Rs 130,000/MT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the unbundling obligation still in force, and what is the role of the independent TSO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PNGRB has withdrawn clause 5A, so no current obligation to unbundle transmission and marketing; the TSO would monitor the 25% third-party open-access quantities on pipelines.

qa_highlights.question: How will depreciation and interest move with new projects commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation about Rs 3,200-3,300 crore in the coming year, with PDH-PP adding about Rs 312 crore; finance cost Rs 310 crore in Q1, about Rs 1,200-1,300 crore annually, with PDH-PP adding about Rs 440 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q4 transmission provision reversed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the provision fell from Rs 111 crore to Rs 11 crore in Q1, and the Q4 one-off was not reversed in the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: Gas marketing PBT guidance for FY27 held at around Rs 4,500 crore despite Q1 PBT of about Rs 3,353 crore; management says it will revise after subsequent quarters if required.
Natural gas transmission volume for FY27 raised to around 123 MMSCMD (from Q1 actual 122.36 MMSCMD), assuming the geopolitical situation continues.

Management expects margin compression in Q2: JCC 9-month average to reflect current Brent to some extent, so Q1-type gas marketing margins may not recur; LPG and petchem profitability expected to decline from Q1 levels.
LHC production expected to stay around 232 TMT range through FY27 with about 1.9 MMSCMD total domestic gas allocation.
Polymer segment expected to reach breakeven during FY27; Pata plant at 100% load.
FY27 capital outlay guidance of around Rs 11,500 crore reiterated; Q1 capex was Rs 6,176 crore.

Depreciation expected around Rs 3,200-3,300 crore in the coming year; finance cost around Rs 1,200-1,300 crore annually, with PDH-PP adding about Rs 312 crore depreciation and about Rs 440 crore finance cost per year.
capex_capacity: Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda pipeline (1,707 km) fully operational from 31 May 2026; Jharsuguda current volume about 0.5 MMSCMD.

JHBDPL remaining section, KKMBPL Phase II, Gurdaspur-Jammu Pipeline and C2-C3 Pipeline scheduled for completion in FY27; Vijaipur-Bina and DUPL-DPPL capacity augmentation in FY28; JLPL capacity augmentation by July 2028.

1,250 KTA PTA plant at GMPL in advanced stage of commissioning; 500 KTA PDH-PP plant expected to be commissioned by June 2027 with completion around December 2027; PDH-PP total cost about Rs 11,256 crore with about Rs 6,000 crore loan.

Three LPG pipelines (Jhansi-Sitarganj 610 km, Cherlapally-Nagpur 556 km, Shikarpur-Hubli-Goa 635 km) authorised by PNGRB on 14 July 2026; total over 1,800 km, investment about Rs 6,700 crore over 3 years.
Two new urea/fertilizer plants under evaluation (Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh) following new urea policy; DFR and investment decisions pending.
GAIL Gas targets about 275 new CNG stations and about 3.70 lakh DPNG connections over the next two years.
Dabhol ambient heating system to be completed by June 2027.
demand_pricing: Gas marketing volume 93.82 MMSCMD including 8.76 MMSCMD international; Qatar force majeure and 7 other cargoes affected, covered by 8 spot cargoes in Q1.

Management says Q1 gas marketing spread was boosted by Henry Hub and JCC 9-month linked sourcing against sales on 3-month dated Brent; sourcing is about 2.4 MMTPA on JCC; about 21 MMSCMD Henry Hub portfolio, roughly half back-to-back, about 20% for Pata, and 25-30% open on cross-index.
Petchem landed gas cost averaged $10.54/MMBtu in Q1; management says breakeven at about $13-14 landed gas cost with selling price around Rs 130,000/MT.
LPG realisation about Rs 90,796/MT in Q1 vs about Rs 54,000 in Q4 (as stated); petchem price about Rs 1,46,000/MT vs Rs 98,000 in Q4; LPG pricing linked to Saudi Aramco index.
LHC inputs: about 1.12 MMSCMD APM gas at around $7/MMBtu and balance new well gas at around $12-13/MMBtu.

Demand: PNGRB paper projects national gas demand rising from about 200 MMSCMD to 297 MMSCMD by FY30; CGD demand about 45-46 MMSCMD to 80-85 MMSCMD by 2030; fertilizer +10-12 MMSCMD; power from about 25-26 to 30-35 MMSCMD.
Transmission volume 122.36 MMSCMD in Q1 vs 118.99 MMSCMD in Q4, with shipper volumes up about 4 MMSCMD. LPG transmission volume 1,077 TMT vs 1,114 TMT in Q4.
Sourcing: 16.5 MMTPA in portfolio; target 7-8 MMTPA by 2030, of which about 2.5 MMTPA sourced.
risks_watch: Gas marketing margin normalisation: JCC 9-month vs 3-month Brent convergence and a fall in dated Brent could reduce the Q2 contribution below the Q1 run rate of about Rs 3,353 crore.
LPG and LHC profitability likely to fall from Q1 as LPG realisation softens; LPG transmission volume affected by West Asia import disruption.
Qatar force majeure and further cargo disruptions requiring spot purchases; management said spot cargoes were sold at reasonable margins.
Polymer segment loss of Rs 130 crore on gas diversion to priority sectors; shift to ethane feedstock for Pata still under pursuit.
PDH-PP timeline slippage (commissioning by June 2027, completion around December 2027) and fertilizer project approvals pending DFR.
Regulatory: PNGRB SUG regulation requiring 3-year-plus sourcing for system-use gas; sourcing plan still being examined.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and demand thesis, but cautious on forward gas marketing and LPG profitability: management repeatedly said Q1 margins were partly one-off and would normalise, and kept FY27 gas marketing guidance unchanged at around Rs 4,500 crore.
